title: Audit pipeline healthchecks & upgrade-aware Terraform module for CloudTrail -> OpenSearch
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a reusable Terraform module that wires CloudTrail -> S3 -> OpenSearch ingestion with defensible retention guardrails, plus built-in synthetic healthchecks and upgrade hooks so Private deployments can be upgraded without losing audit continuity. The module must be idempotent across repeated applies, have clear state migration guidance, and expose observability surfaces (metrics/logs) for Console to show ingestion health and retention posture.
acceptance_criteria: Module implements CloudTrail setup (trail, multi-region option) with configurable S3 bucket and lifecycle rules that support 'hot' (OpenSearch) and 'cold' (Glacier) tiers

OpenSearch ingestion pipeline resources (index templates, ingest pipelines, ILM policies) are created idempotently and support a migration toggle to new ILM policies without reindexing if retention windows change
A lightweight synthetic event generator and validator is included and can be scheduled via EventBridge/Lambda to exercise end-to-end path once the module is instantiated
Terraform plan/apply does not destroy + recreate buckets or OpenSearch domains during minor module upgrades by default (upgrade hooks and lifecycle rules applied)
Module exposes Prometheus-style metrics (CloudWatch metric filters + SNS alarm subscriptions) for: last-successful-ingest-timestamp, ingest-error-rate, s3-put-latency-percentile
Comprehensive docs and migration steps included in README with examples for single-account and cross-account ingestion, and a sample Canary dashboard in Console
implementation_notes: Prefer separate smaller resources instead of monolithic resource with complex lifecycle: S3 bucket + separate lifecycle rules resources, CloudTrail resource, OpenSearch resources and IAM roles.
Use Terraform 1.5+ features and provider pinning. Keep state migration steps explicit: use 'terraform state mv' examples in README for renaming resources introduced in earlier versions.
Provide optional 'external_manifest' input so customers can supply pre-existing index templates or ingest pipelines to avoid reindexing during upgrades.

Add a boolean 'enable_canary' that deploys a small scheduled Lambda (node/python) that emits a structured audit event and validates it appears in OpenSearch; Lambda writes its result to CloudWatch and a CloudWatch metric is emitted for Console to scrape.

ILM policy creation should provide a 'policy_version' tag. When incremented, module creates new ILM policy and an alias-based rollover strategy; include doced manual migration path for reindexing if needed. Avoid automatic reindex on upgrade.
S3 lifecycle rules must be explicit about noncurrent version expiration and abort-incomplete-multipart-upload to avoid storage surprises.
Use 'lifecycle' ignore_changes for OpenSearch domain capacity fields where dangerous changes would force replacement; surface warnings in outputs if user changes those fields.
Cross-account CloudTrail ingestion should use a centralized ingest account pattern with documented IAM trust assumptions and example 'assume_role' policies.
migration_plan: Phase 1: Alpha deploy to dev VPC - deploy module with minimal options and enable_canary=true. Verify synthetic events arrive and metrics emit.
Phase 2: Staged rollout to 2 internal test accounts. Validate retention behavior for >30d, confirm ILM policies created and old indices maintain read alias.
Phase 3: Run a dry-run state migration with 'terraform state mv' for renamed S3 resources on 1 customer-like environment. Document exact CLI commands and pre/post checks.
Phase 4: Production rollout with 48h monitoring window. Keep previous module version available and disable automatic destructive changes in plan via pre-apply review checklist.

Rollback plan: Use Terraform plan outputs to identify resource replacements. If OpenSearch domain replacement required, stop canary, snapshot indices, restore to a new domain, and repoint ingest role.
test_plan: Unit tests: Terratest / kitchen-terraform to validate plan for common permutations (single-account, cross-account, enable_canary toggled).
Integration: Deploy to ephemeral AWS account, run canary for 24h, assert canary metric stable and ingestion latency < 30s for test events.
Chaos test: Simulate OpenSearch ingestion failures (throttle/503) and watch module alarms trigger; confirm canary alerts and documented operator runbook exercise.
Upgrade test: Apply current module version, then apply upgraded module with ILM policy version bump; ensure no index loss and new policy available for new indices only.
Security test: Verify least-privilege IAM roles for Lambda/cross-account assume role. Conduct basic static analysis on Lambda code for secrets handling.
risks: OpenSearch domain replacement on misconfiguration could cause downtime—mitigated by ignore_changes and explicit warnings in outputs.
Automatic ILM changes can inadvertently shorten retention; mitigation: policy_versioning and manual opt-in migration steps.
Cross-account role assumptions are error-prone; provide templated trust policy and troubleshooting checklist.
Synthetic canary adds a slight noise to audit logs; make it easily filterable via a dedicated source event field.
